summary:
Imagine an astronaut aboard a spacecraft, millions of kilometres away from Earth. Suddenly, their vital signs begin showing unusual patterns. Mission control cannot respond immediately, and instant medical assistance is not an option. In the vastness of space, even a communication delay can make a critical difference.

AstroVitals is designed to address this challenge by bringing intelligent health monitoring and mission support into a unified platform. It combines crew biometric monitoring, AI-assisted health assessment, automated alerts, and environmental monitoring to help identify potential health concerns and provide better visibility into crew well-being.

But AstroVitals goes beyond conventional health-monitoring systems. Its strongest differentiator is its communication-delay-aware mission workflow. It allows health snapshots to be queued and medical communication drafts to be prepared and stored locally, ensuring that important health information is not dependent on an immediate connection to Earth.

Using a hybrid AI architecture and simulated telemetry, AstroVitals demonstrates how intelligent monitoring can support more autonomous healthcare during space missions.

Ultimately, AstroVitals aims to make long-duration space exploration safer and more resilient by reducing dependence on continuous communication with Earth and helping ensure that critical health information remains accessible, even in the most isolated environments.
details:
Astronauts aboard a spacecraft float millions of kilometres away from Earth. A sudden change in their vital signs raises concerns, but communication with mission control could be delayed. In an environment where immediate medical assistance cannot always be guaranteed, monitoring crew health and preserving critical medical information becomes esssential.

AstroVitals is a health monitoring and mission tool for astronauts in space. It features a dashboard to monitor and evaluate simulated astronaut health, including vital signs, environment variables, and alerts.

It tracks multiple vital signs of astronauts such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, breating rate, temperature and Hear Rate Variability. The backend uses rale based health classificiations and threshold based anomalies to highlight any potentially anamalous readings and evaluate their health. It also includes profile information on each crew memeber, trends int heir health, management of alerts and downloadable health reports.

An important feature of this project is it accounts for delays in communication during missions. This means you can queue up health updates and draft messages to send to medical professionals.

This tool was built using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The backend was created using Node.js and Express.js. Data was stoed using SQLite. Health evaluations were done using JavaScript. Simulated telemetry was used to show different scenarios. The application was deployede using Vercel.

This tool goes beyond a standard health monitoring dashboard by considering the practical issues faced with provifing healthcare in isolated situations. The tool has been designed with modularity in mind meaning there is potential to integrate real health sensors, trained machine learning models, long term data storage and real communications in the future.

Overall this tool aims to help provide a safer and more independent space exploration by making it easier to monitor, evaluate and store health information of the crew.
